blueprint_topic: Management of Care — evaluating outcomes of multidisciplinary heart-failure disease management
stem: A health system is evaluating a multidisciplinary heart-failure disease-management program that includes coordinated follow-up, self-care education, and adherence support. Which finding is most consistent with the AHA/ACC/HFSA evidence summary?

options.A: The program may reduce heart-failure hospitalizations, while self-care interventions can also improve quality of life and other selected outcomes.
options.B: The program should be considered ineffective unless it produces a measurable reduction in every clinical outcome tracked by the health system.
options.C: The program is expected to improve education and transition measures, but hospitalization outcomes are not affected by multidisciplinary follow-up.
options.D: The program should replace usual longitudinal clinicians because the benefits of multidisciplinary care depend on using a single centralized team.

rationale: A is correct. The 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline summarizes meta-analyses showing that multidisciplinary interventions and specialized multidisciplinary follow-up can reduce heart-failure and all-cause hospitalizations, while self-care interventions can reduce heart-failure-related hospitalization and improve quality of life. The guideline also describes case-management and team-based programs as coordinated care across settings rather than a replacement for all usual clinicians. B is incorrect because the evidence does not require every tracked outcome to improve for a program to be beneficial; some interventions improve transition quality or quality of life without significantly changing all clinical outcomes. C is incorrect because reduced hospitalization is specifically reported in multiple multidisciplinary and self-care evidence summaries. D is incorrect because these programs are multidisciplinary coordination models and do not depend on replacing usual longitudinal clinicians with a single centralized team.
educational_objective: Recognize that multidisciplinary heart-failure disease-management and self-care interventions can improve selected outcomes such as hospitalization risk and quality of life, without implying that every program improves every outcome or replaces ongoing longitudinal care.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_version_date: Originally published April 1, 2022 with subsequent corrections; still listed on the current ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub when rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Section 7.1.1 Self-Care Support in HF — Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 1: multidisciplinary interventions and specialized multidisciplinary follow-up were associated with reduced hospital admission/HF hospitalization/all-cause hospitalization; case-management and multidisciplinary interventions reduced readmission outcomes. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 2: self-care interventions reduced HF-related and all-cause hospitalization and improved quality of life; some transitional-care education improved discharge preparedness, transition quality, and QOL without significantly improving all clinical outcomes. Section 9.6 Integration of Care: Transitions and Team-Based Approaches describes disease-management programs as coordinated multidisciplinary care across settings. ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub continues to list the 2022 guideline as the current HF guideline resource.
source_claim_supported: Current HF guidance supports multidisciplinary/case-management and self-care interventions as strategies associated with reduced HF-related hospitalization and improved quality of life or other selected outcomes, while also showing that not every intervention improves every clinical endpoint.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Performance Improvement, Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Concepts of Management, and Continuity of Care: participate in quality-improvement processes; evaluate management outcomes; collaborate across disciplines; coordinate/manage care; follow up unresolved client-care issues.
pdf_visual_verification: Relevant NCSBN Management of Care content was visually verified on PDF pages 24–25/file pages 25–26 earlier in this 2026-08-20 audit session; no CACHE MISS for the Performance Improvement/Collaboration locators used here. The HF guideline was verified through current HTML/ACC hub pages; no guideline PDF is relied upon for the item.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'heart failure multidisciplinary disease management hospitalization quality of life self care program outcomes' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the outcomes-evaluation construct but removed the two 'only' distractors and the uniquely long key. The revised item avoids promising universal benefit and instead tests realistic misinterpretations: requiring improvement in every outcome, denying hospitalization effects, and treating team-based care as a replacement for longitudinal clinicians.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly reflects guideline evidence for reduced hospitalization and improved QOL/selected outcomes while preserving uncertainty across individual programs and endpoints.
option_audit.B: Plausible overstrict evaluation error; incorrect because programs may improve selected outcomes without improving every endpoint.
option_audit.C: Plausible transition-only misconception; incorrect because hospitalization reductions are directly reported in the multidisciplinary/self-care evidence summaries.
option_audit.D: Plausible centralized-program misconception; incorrect because guideline-supported disease management coordinates multidisciplinary care across settings rather than replacing all ongoing clinicians.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable outcome-evaluation detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel interpretations of program outcomes and structure.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ACC/HFSA source-based reread.
